info.title: Pricewise — Dynamic Pricing Intelligence API
info.description:
REST API for the multi-tenant, multi-agent dynamic pricing platform.

**Four rules apply to every endpoint below.**

1. **Auth is a cookie, not a bearer token.** `POST /auth/login` sets an
   httpOnly `access_token` (15 min, path `/`) and `refresh_token` (path
   `/auth`). The browser sends them automatically. JavaScript never sees
   them, so there is no `Authorization` header anywhere in this document.

2. **Every state-changing request must send `X-Pricewise-Client`.** Any
   value will do. A cross-site HTML form cannot set a custom header, so
   requiring one rejects forged submissions before they reach a handler.
   Omit it on a POST, PATCH, PUT or DELETE and you get **403
   `CSRF_REQUIRED`**, whatever else is correct about the request.

3. **One envelope, always.** Success is
   `{ success: true, data, pagination? }`; failure is
   `{ success: false, error: { code, message, details? } }`. No endpoint
   returns a bare array, a bare string, or a value outside `data`.
   `details` is omitted entirely when empty rather than sent as null.

4. **Another tenant's resource returns 404, not 403.** A 403 would confirm
   the row exists, which is itself a leak. Every tenant-scoped query is
   filtered by the `orgId` on the verified JWT, and a client-supplied
   `organizationId` in a body or query is stripped and logged.

All LLM calls happen server-side. The browser never talks to Groq.

servers.description: Production. Render's free tier spins down after about fifteen minutes idle, so the first request can take roughly 35 seconds.

post.summary: Create a new organization and its first admin user

post.summary: Rotate the refresh token and issue a new access token
post.description: Refresh tokens rotate on use, so a replayed token is treated as theft and revokes the whole chain. The client must therefore serialise refreshes; five queries failing with 401 at once must produce one refresh, not five.

401.description: Refresh token missing, expired, or revoked

post.summary: Trigger the 5-agent pricing pipeline for this product
post.description:
Runs the five agents and streams their progress as Server-Sent Events.
Takes roughly 8 to 12 seconds against the live model.

**This is a POST, not an `EventSource`.** It needs the CSRF header and
a request body cannot ride on `EventSource`, so a client reads the
response body as a stream instead.

**Events are named**, so a client must use `addEventListener(name)`,
not `onmessage`. Six names exist. Every payload also repeats its name
in a `type` field, so a single parser can switch on the body alone:

| Event | Payload |
|---|---|
| `agent_started` | `{ type, agent, startedAt }` |
| `agent_completed` | `{ type, agent, durationMs, confidence, output, toolCalls, promptTokens, completionTokens }` |
| `agent_skipped` | `{ type, agent, reason }` |
| `agent_failed` | `{ type, agent, error, willRetry }` |
| `recommendation_ready` | `{ type, autoExecuted, recommendationId, blocked?, executionFailed? }` |
| `recommendation_failed` | `{ type, error, failedAgent? }` |

`recommendation_ready` carries an **id, not the recommendation**. Fetch
`GET /recommendations/{id}` for the full object.

**Order.** `MARKET_INTELLIGENCE` and `INVENTORY_COST` start together;
their `agent_started` events share a timestamp. `DEMAND_FORECASTING`,
`PRICING_STRATEGY` and `EXECUTION_COMPLIANCE` then run in sequence,
because each needs the one before it.

**Failure is in-band.** The stream always returns 200 once it has
opened, because headers are already flushed by the time an agent can
fail. A pipeline failure arrives as `recommendation_failed`, never as a
4xx or 5xx. Check the events, not the status.

A `: keep-alive` comment frame is sent every 15 seconds so proxies do
not close an idle connection. Ignore it. Responses carry
`Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no`;
any proxy in front of this must also disable buffering or the whole
stream arrives at once at the end, which defeats the point.

Disconnecting does not abort the run. The pipeline finishes and the
recommendation is persisted either way.

schema.description: Newline-delimited SSE frames, one JSON object per data line.

404.description: No such product in this organization

get.summary: Get full detail including every agent's individual contribution

post.summary: Approve a pending recommendation (Pricing Analyst or Admin)

200.description: Approved and executed against the mock e-commerce API

post.summary: Reject a pending recommendation with a reason
Override the recommended price with a manually chosen price
Revert a decision, putting the recommendation back to PENDING
post.description: Backs out an approve, reject or modify and restores the previous price on the platform. This is what the toast's Undo calls. It is bounded: only the user who resolved it can undo it, and only while it is the most recent execution for that product.

200.description: Reverted, and back in the queue

404.description: Not found, or belongs to another organization

409.description: Already undone, still pending, or superseded by a later price change. CONFLICT.

post.summary: Approve several pending recommendations in one request
post.description: Partial success is the normal case, so this never fails as a whole. Each id gets its own result and the caller is told plainly how many went through. A recommendation another request resolved first comes back as not ok rather than silently counting as approved.

200.description: One result per id, in the order supplied

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Matches action, entityType and an entityId prefix. Deliberately not the actor's name: the name is resolved after the page is read, from the organization's members, so it is not a column to filter on. Filter by userId instead.

get.summary: Distinct action names present in this organization's audit trail
get.description: Populates the Activity filter without the client hardcoding a list.

Deliberately NOT wrapped in the success envelope, because it is consumed by platform health checks rather than by the client. Groq being unavailable is degraded rather than dead: the catalog, queue, activity and settings all still work, so only generation is affected and the check stays green.

post.summary: Mock of the storefront's price-update endpoint
post.description:
Stands in for the external e-commerce platform. Called by the Execution and Compliance agent, never by the frontend. Simulates latency and an induced failure rate so the rollback path is exercised rather than assumed.

**Unauthenticated, deliberately.** It is mounted outside `requireAuth` because it represents a third-party system, not part of this API's tenant surface. Nothing behind it reads tenant data: it takes a SKU and a price and returns a receipt. In a real deployment this is someone else's endpoint behind their own credentials.

200.description: Price updated on the mock platform

502.description: Simulated platform failure — caller must roll back

ClientHeader.name: X-Pricewise-Client
ClientHeader.description: Required on every state-changing verb. Any non-empty value. Missing it is a 403 CSRF_REQUIRED. See rule 2 in the description above.

details.description: Field-level errors, keyed by field name.

confidenceThreshold.description: At or above this, a recommendation executes without a human. Below it, the recommendation goes to the approval queue.

maxPriceDeltaPct.description: Largest single price move allowed, as a fraction.

factorWeights.description: The four factors the strategy agent weighted, summing to 1.

ToolCall.description: One tool the model chose to call, with the arguments it chose.

AgentRun.description: One agent invocation, persisted whether it succeeded or failed. This is the explainability record: it carries the tool calls the model decided to make, which is what lets a reviewer see how a price was reached.

comparable.description: Past decisions on similar products, for context.
